title: Choosing a University
passage: Choosing a university is one of the most important decisions a young person makes. Many students focus only on academic rankings, but experts suggest considering other factors as well. The location of the campus, the cost of living, and the availability of internships can all shape a student's experience. One graduate said that the city where she studied offered her more opportunities than the university's reputation ever did.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Academic ranking is the only important factor
Students should consider many factors when choosing a university
Internships are more important than studying
questions.explanation: 文章强调选择大学不应只看排名，还要考虑位置、生活费、实习机会等因素。

questions.question: What factor does the graduate mention as most valuable?
questions.explanation: 毕业生说，她学习的城市带给她的机会比学校名声更多。

questions.question: Which factor is NOT mentioned in the passage?
questions.explanation: 文中提到位置、生活费和实习机会，未提及体育设施。

title: The Benefits of Walking
passage: Walking is often overlooked as a form of exercise, yet it is one of the healthiest activities available. Doctors say that thirty minutes of brisk walking each day can reduce the risk of heart disease and improve mood. Unlike running, walking puts little pressure on the joints, making it suitable for people of all ages. Best of all, it requires no special equipment and can be done almost anywhere.

questions.question: How long should people walk each day according to the passage?
questions.explanation: 医生说每天快走三十分钟即可降低心脏病风险。

questions.question: Why is walking suitable for people of all ages?
options: It puts little pressure on the joints
It burns more calories than running
questions.explanation: 走路对关节压力小，因此适合各年龄段的人。

questions.question: What is one advantage of walking mentioned in the passage?
options: It can be done almost anywhere
It is only for young people
questions.explanation: 文中提到走路不需要特殊装备，几乎在任何地方都能进行。

title: The History of Tea
passage: Tea has been enjoyed for thousands of years and is now the second most popular drink in the world after water. According to legend, tea was discovered in China when leaves blew into a pot of boiling water. From China, the habit of drinking tea spread to Japan and then, through traders, to Europe. Today, tea is grown in dozens of countries and prepared in countless different ways.

questions.question: What is the second most popular drink in the world?
questions.explanation: 茶是世界上仅次于水的第二大饮品。

questions.question: How was tea discovered according to the legend?
options: A trader brought it from Europe
Scientists created it in a lab
questions.explanation: 传说中，茶叶被风吹进煮沸的水里，从而发现了茶。

questions.question: Which country did tea spread to first after China?
questions.explanation: 茶先从中国传到日本，再经商人传到欧洲。

title: Why We Dream
passage: Scientists still do not fully understand why we dream, but they have several theories. One theory suggests that dreams help us process emotions and memories from the day. Another proposes that dreaming is simply the brain's way of staying active during sleep. What is certain is that everyone dreams, even people who claim they never remember their dreams. On average, a person dreams for about two hours every night.

questions.question: What is one theory about why we dream?
options: Dreams help process emotions and memories
Dreams only happen to some people
questions.explanation: 一种理论认为梦帮助我们处理白天的情绪和记忆。

questions.question: How long does a person dream each night on average?
questions.explanation: 人们平均每晚做梦约两小时。

questions.question: What is certain about dreaming?
questions.explanation: 可以确定的是每个人都会做梦，即使有些人声称从不记得。

title: The Rise of Online Shopping
passage: Online shopping has grown rapidly over the past two decades, transforming the way people buy goods. Consumers now enjoy the convenience of ordering almost anything from home and having it delivered to their door. However, this convenience has come at a cost for traditional stores, many of which have closed. Economists note that while prices online are often lower, shoppers should still compare products carefully and be aware of delivery fees.

questions.question: What has online shopping transformed?
questions.explanation: 网上购物改变了人们购买商品的方式。

questions.question: What happened to many traditional stores?
questions.explanation: 网购的便利让许多传统商店关门了。

questions.question: What do economists advise shoppers to do?
options: Compare products and watch for delivery fees
questions.explanation: 经济学家提醒消费者要仔细比较商品，并注意运费。

title: The Importance of Breakfast
passage: Breakfast is often called the most important meal of the day, and research appears to support this. Studies show that people who eat breakfast tend to concentrate better at work and school. Skipping breakfast, on the other hand, can lead to low energy and overeating later in the day. Nutritionists recommend a breakfast that includes protein, whole grains, and fruit for a balanced start to the morning.

questions.question: What do studies show about people who eat breakfast?
questions.explanation: 研究表明吃早餐的人在工作学习中注意力更集中。

questions.question: What can skipping breakfast lead to?
questions.explanation: 不吃早餐可能导致精力不足和之后暴饮暴食。

questions.question: What do nutritionists recommend for breakfast?
questions.explanation: 营养师建议早餐包含蛋白质、全谷物和水果。

title: Learning a Musical Instrument
passage: Learning to play a musical instrument offers benefits that go far beyond the ability to perform. Children who study music often develop better memory and discipline. Playing an instrument also teaches patience, because progress comes slowly and through regular practice. Even adults who begin late in life report that music brings them joy and relaxation. Many schools, however, have cut music programmes due to budget pressures, which experts describe as shortsighted.

questions.question: What is one benefit of learning music mentioned in the passage?
questions.explanation: 学习音乐的孩子往往记忆力更好、更有纪律。

questions.question: What does playing an instrument teach?
questions.explanation: 演奏乐器教会人耐心，因为进步是缓慢的。

questions.question: Why have many schools cut music programmes?
questions.explanation: 由于预算压力，许多学校削减了音乐课程。

title: The Sharing Economy
passage: The sharing economy has grown from a niche idea into a global industry worth billions of dollars. Services that allow people to rent homes, cars, and tools from one another have made better use of resources that would otherwise sit idle. Supporters argue that this model reduces waste and creates flexible income. Critics, however, point out that it has disrupted traditional industries and raised concerns about regulation and worker protection.

questions.question: What does the sharing economy allow people to do?
questions.explanation: 共享经济让人们互相租用房屋、汽车和工具。

questions.question: What do supporters say about the sharing economy?
options: It reduces waste and creates income
questions.explanation: 支持者认为它减少浪费并创造灵活收入。

questions.question: What concern do critics raise?
questions.explanation: 批评者担心监管和工人保护问题。

title: The Effects of Sleep Deprivation
passage: Sleep deprivation has become a widespread problem in modern society, where long working hours and constant screen time push sleep to the bottom of the priority list. The effects are more serious than many realise. Lack of sleep impairs attention and memory, weakens the immune system, and increases the risk of serious illness. Researchers stress that consistently sleeping fewer than seven hours a night is linked to long-term health problems, and they urge people to treat sleep as a necessity rather than a luxury.

questions.question: What is a major cause of sleep deprivation mentioned in the passage?
options: Long working hours and screen time
questions.explanation: 长时间工作和持续的屏幕使用把睡眠挤到了优先级的最后。

questions.question: What is one effect of lack of sleep?
questions.explanation: 睡眠不足会削弱免疫系统。

questions.question: How many hours of sleep is linked to long-term health problems?
questions.explanation: 研究人员指出，长期每晚睡不到七小时与健康问题相关。

title: Urban Green Spaces
passage: As cities grow denser, the value of urban green spaces becomes increasingly clear. Parks and tree-lined streets do more than beautify a neighbourhood; they cool the surrounding air, absorb rainwater, and provide habitats for wildlife. Studies also link access to green space with lower levels of stress and better mental health. Despite these benefits, green space is often the first thing to be sacrificed when land is scarce, a decision planners increasingly regret.

questions.question: What is one physical benefit of urban green spaces?
questions.explanation: 绿地和林荫道能降低周围空气温度。

questions.question: What do studies link green space to?
questions.explanation: 研究把接触绿地与压力降低和更好的心理健康联系起来。

questions.question: What happens when land is scarce?
questions.explanation: 土地稀缺时，绿地往往首先被牺牲。

title: The Digital Divide
passage: The digital divide refers to the gap between those who have access to modern technology and those who do not. This divide exists not only between rich and poor countries but also within them, affecting the elderly, rural residents, and low-income families. During the pandemic, when education and work moved online, the divide became painfully visible, as students without reliable internet struggled to keep up. Closing this gap, experts argue, is essential for building a fair society.

questions.question: What does the digital divide refer to?
questions.explanation: 数字鸿沟指能接触现代技术的人与不能的人之间的差距。

questions.question: Who is affected by the digital divide?
options: The elderly, rural residents and low-income families
questions.explanation: 鸿沟影响老年人、农村居民和低收入家庭。

questions.question: When did the divide become painfully visible?
questions.explanation: 疫情期间教育和办公转为线上，数字鸿沟变得显而易见。

title: The Psychology of Gratitude
passage: Psychologists have found that gratitude is one of the simplest and most effective ways to improve well-being. People who regularly write down things they are thankful for report higher life satisfaction and fewer symptoms of depression. The practice works by shifting attention away from what is missing and toward what is already present. Experts recommend making gratitude a daily habit, such as noting three good things before going to bed.

questions.question: What is gratitude according to the passage?
options: An effective way to improve well-being
questions.explanation: 感恩是改善幸福感最简单有效的方法之一。

questions.question: How does gratitude work?
options: By shifting attention to what is present
questions.explanation: 感恩通过把注意力从缺失转移到已有而发挥作用。

questions.question: What do experts recommend before bed?
questions.explanation: 专家建议睡前记下三件好事。

title: The Decline of Handwriting
passage: As keyboards and touchscreens replace pens, handwriting is quietly disappearing from daily life. This change carries unexpected consequences. Research shows that writing by hand activates areas of the brain involved in memory and learning in ways that typing does not. Students who take notes by hand tend to understand and retain material better than those who type. Some educators therefore argue that handwriting should remain part of the curriculum, not out of nostalgia, but for its genuine cognitive benefits.

questions.question: What is quietly disappearing from daily life?
questions.explanation: 随着键盘和触屏取代笔，手写正从日常生活中消失。

questions.question: What does writing by hand activate?
options: Areas of the brain involved in memory
questions.explanation: 手写能激活大脑中与记忆和学习相关的区域。

questions.question: Why do some educators want to keep handwriting in the curriculum?
questions.explanation: 教育者认为应保留手写，是因为它真正的认知益处而非怀旧。

title: The Economics of Happiness
passage: The relationship between money and happiness is more complicated than most people assume. Research shows that rising income does improve well-being, but only up to a point. Once basic needs are met, additional wealth produces smaller and smaller gains in satisfaction. What predicts happiness far more reliably are relationships, health, and a sense of purpose. This finding has led some governments to look beyond economic growth and to measure the well-being of their citizens directly.

questions.question: According to the passage, rising income improves well-being only until what point?
questions.explanation: 收入增长只在基本需求满足之前显著提升幸福感。

questions.question: What predicts happiness more reliably than money?
questions.explanation: 关系、健康和目标感比金钱更能预测幸福。

questions.question: What have some governments begun to measure?
questions.explanation: 一些政府开始直接衡量公民的幸福感。

title: The Rise of Remote Work
passage: Remote work, once a rare perk, has become a permanent feature of many industries. Employees value the flexibility it offers, saving hours previously spent commuting and gaining more control over their schedules. Employers have also noticed benefits, including access to a wider talent pool and lower office costs. However, remote work is not without challenges. Some workers report feelings of isolation, and managers struggle to build team culture across a screen.

questions.question: What do employees value about remote work?
questions.explanation: 员工看重远程工作的灵活性，节省通勤时间。

questions.question: What benefit do employers notice?
options: Access to a wider talent pool
questions.explanation: 雇主发现远程工作能接触到更广泛的人才库并降低办公成本。

questions.question: What challenge is mentioned in the passage?
questions.explanation: 一些员工报告感到孤立，管理者难以隔着屏幕建立团队文化。

title: Why We Procrastinate
passage: Procrastination is often mistaken for laziness, but psychologists see it differently. They describe it as an emotional problem rather than a time-management problem. When a task triggers anxiety or boredom, the brain seeks relief by turning to something more pleasant, and this short-term escape only makes the task loom larger. Breaking the cycle, experts say, begins with forgiving yourself for past delays and starting with a task so small that beginning feels easy.

questions.question: How do psychologists describe procrastination?
questions.explanation: 心理学家把拖延描述为情绪问题而非时间管理问题。

questions.question: Why does the brain turn to something more pleasant?
questions.explanation: 当任务引发焦虑或无聊时，大脑通过转向更愉快的事来寻求缓解。

questions.question: What is the first step to breaking the cycle?
questions.explanation: 专家说打破循环始于原谅自己过去的拖延。

title: The Benefits of Bilingualism
passage: Bilingualism was once viewed with suspicion, but research has turned that view on its head. Far from confusing the mind, speaking two languages appears to strengthen it. Bilingual individuals constantly manage two linguistic systems, which exercises the brain's executive control and improves attention. Some studies even suggest that lifelong bilingualism may delay the onset of dementia by several years, building a cognitive reserve that protects the ageing brain.

questions.question: How was bilingualism once viewed?
questions.explanation: 双语能力曾被怀疑地看待。

questions.question: What does speaking two languages strengthen?
questions.explanation: 双语者不断管理两套语言系统，锻炼了大脑的执行控制能力。

questions.question: What may lifelong bilingualism delay?
questions.explanation: 研究表明终身双语可能将痴呆症发病推迟数年。

title: Food Waste
passage: About a third of all food produced worldwide is never eaten. This waste occurs at every stage, from farms where crops are rejected for cosmetic flaws, to homes where leftovers are thrown away. The environmental cost is enormous, since wasted food consumes land, water, and energy, and its decomposition releases greenhouse gases. Reducing food waste, experts argue, is one of the most effective actions individuals can take to fight climate change, starting with simple habits like planning meals and using leftovers.

questions.question: How much of the world's food is never eaten?
questions.explanation: 全球约三分之一的食物从未被食用。

questions.question: Why are crops rejected on farms?
options: For being too small to pick
questions.explanation: 农作物因外观瑕疵而被丢弃。

questions.question: What is a simple habit to reduce food waste?
questions.explanation: 规划膳食和利用剩菜是减少浪费的简单习惯。

title: The Growth Mindset
passage: The growth mindset is the belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning. People with this mindset tend to see challenges as opportunities rather than threats, and they persist longer when facing difficulty. In contrast, those with a fixed mindset believe that intelligence is innate and unchangeable, which can lead them to avoid challenges for fear of failure. The key insight, educators say, is that praising effort rather than talent encourages the kind of persistence that leads to genuine improvement.

questions.question: What is the growth mindset?
options: The belief that abilities can be developed
The belief that intelligence is fixed
questions.explanation: 成长型思维是相信能力可以通过努力和学习发展。

questions.question: What do people with a fixed mindset tend to do?
options: Avoid challenges for fear of failure
questions.explanation: 固定型思维的人认为智力天生不变，可能因害怕失败而回避挑战。

questions.question: What should educators praise to encourage persistence?
questions.explanation: 教育者应表扬努力而非天赋，以鼓励坚持。

title: The History of the Internet
passage: The internet began as a research project in the 1960s, designed to allow computers at different locations to share information. At the time, few imagined it would become the global network it is today. Over the following decades, it expanded from universities and research centres to homes and businesses around the world. The arrival of the World Wide Web in the early 1990s made the internet accessible to ordinary people, and it has since transformed communication, commerce, and culture.

questions.question: When did the internet begin?
questions.explanation: 互联网始于 20 世纪 60 年代的研究项目。

questions.question: What was the original purpose of the internet?
questions.explanation: 互联网最初是为了让不同地点的计算机共享信息。

questions.question: What made the internet accessible to ordinary people?
questions.explanation: 20 世纪 90 年代初万维网的出现让普通人也能使用互联网。

title: The Power of Reading Aloud
passage: Reading aloud is often considered an activity for children, but it benefits people of all ages. When we read aloud, we engage both the visual and auditory parts of the brain, which deepens comprehension and memory. Language learners, in particular, benefit from hearing the rhythm and pronunciation of words. Teachers recommend reading aloud for just a few minutes each day, noting that the practice improves fluency and builds confidence over time.

questions.question: Who benefits from reading aloud?
questions.explanation: 朗读对所有年龄段的人都有益。

questions.question: Why does reading aloud deepen comprehension?
options: It engages visual and auditory parts of the brain
questions.explanation: 朗读同时调动大脑的视觉和听觉部分，加深理解和记忆。

questions.question: How long do teachers recommend reading aloud?
questions.explanation: 教师建议每天朗读几分钟即可。

title: The Science of Smell
passage: Of all the senses, smell is perhaps the most closely linked to memory. A single scent can instantly recall a childhood kitchen or a long-forgotten holiday. Scientists explain that this is because the brain region that processes smell sits directly next to the areas responsible for emotion and memory. This close connection is why certain smells trigger vivid recollections that other senses cannot match, a phenomenon sometimes called the Proust effect.

questions.question: Which sense is most closely linked to memory?
questions.explanation: 嗅觉是与记忆联系最紧密的感官。

questions.question: Why do smells trigger vivid memories?
options: The smell region is next to emotion and memory areas
questions.explanation: 处理嗅觉的大脑区域紧邻负责情绪和记忆的区域。

questions.question: What is this phenomenon sometimes called?
questions.explanation: 这一现象有时被称为普鲁斯特效应。

title: Volunteering and Well-being
passage: Volunteering is usually described in terms of what it gives to others, but research shows that volunteers themselves gain a great deal. Studies find that people who volunteer regularly report better mental health, lower stress, and a stronger sense of belonging. Helping others appears to activate the same reward systems in the brain that respond to other pleasures, leading some researchers to call volunteering a natural mood enhancer.

questions.question: How is volunteering usually described?
options: In terms of what it gives to others
questions.explanation: 志愿服务通常被描述为给予他人。

questions.question: What do regular volunteers report?
questions.explanation: 定期做志愿者的人报告更好的心理健康、更低的压力和更强的归属感。

questions.question: What do some researchers call volunteering?
questions.explanation: 帮助他人激活大脑的奖赏系统，研究者称之为天然的情绪提升剂。

title: The Importance of Critical Thinking
passage: In an age of information overload, critical thinking has become an essential skill. It is the ability to evaluate evidence, question assumptions, and distinguish fact from opinion. Schools have traditionally focused on delivering knowledge, but educators increasingly argue that teaching students how to think is more important than teaching them what to think. A person who can think critically is less easily misled and better equipped to make sound decisions in a complex world.

questions.question: What is critical thinking?
questions.explanation: 批判性思维是评估证据、质疑假设和区分事实与观点的能力。

questions.question: What do educators increasingly argue?
options: Teaching how to think is more important than what to think
questions.explanation: 教育者认为教学生如何思考比教他们思考什么更重要。

questions.question: What is a benefit of critical thinking?
questions.explanation: 能批判性思考的人不易被误导，更能做出明智的决定。

title: The Value of Failure
passage: Failure is rarely welcome, yet it is one of the most effective teachers. Many of history's greatest achievements were built on repeated setbacks, from scientific discoveries to entrepreneurial success. The key difference between those who grow from failure and those who are defeated by it lies in how they respond. People who examine their mistakes, learn from them, and try again tend to build the resilience that eventually leads to success. In this sense, failure is not the opposite of success but a necessary step on the road to it.

questions.question: What is one of the most effective teachers according to the passage?
questions.explanation: 失败是最有效的老师之一。

questions.question: What is the key difference between those who grow and those who are defeated?
questions.explanation: 关键区别在于人们如何回应失败。

questions.question: What does failure eventually lead to for those who learn from it?
questions.explanation: 从失败中学习的人会培养出最终通向成功的韧性。
